spiritual_reading:
After the Divine life had brought the ordered heavens and their lower forms into being, it turned itself toward the outermost degree and established its presence there. It gave an indication to the Divine that rules by truth, and the ordered progressions of states were set in motion and lifted into a higher arrangement. Then a general influx of truth was extended into those progressions, and an inbreathing of life entered them, and their activities were aroused. By this influx the outermost degree was purified by truths.

And the impure remainder and encrustation of the full complex of mixed influences—those derived from falsified truth, from denial of good, and from perverted love—which had flowed down into the outermost degree, were gathered up and confined within the general store of external knowledges that is held inside boundaries and containing forms. Because this general store received what was harsh from the cleansing of those mixed influences, the knowledges there became savorless to spiritual taste and were made bitter.

When the Divine life ascended toward higher states, it released the ordered progression of cognitions that govern times and changes. It purified that progression and loosened all the thickened falsity within it, and cast that loosened remainder down into the same general external repository, from an elevated state into an external one. The remainder from that purification was mingled into those general knowledges. A ruling intention within that repository drew the scattered remainder together; and that intention gathered and bound it so that it became fixed.

Upon this fixed composite, the measurements of successive states were impressed: the distinctions of lesser changes and greater changes, the full cycles of progression, and the determinations of cognitions with their ordered varieties. It came into being from these determinations, was separated from their active government, and was confined within the general external repository. Upon the whole of this composite were impressed the images, the fixed patterns, the appearances, the persuasive teachings, and the deliberations that had remained from the former progression, because it was the condensed residue of them all. Therefore, whenever any cognition shines forth or any ordered variety turns into effect, this composite serves, for one, as an incitement and, for another, as a confirmation.

It was cast into that external repository in the same way that a general influx pours down and is received into what is common. It was forced into that state wholly by the operation and governance of ministering powers. It was carried down to the place of grinding and formation, where the ordered whole had been established in its outer workings; and the general external repository also received it and took part in its formation, being the chief agent in giving it determinate shape. It formed it into a representative likeness, and it was altered more than the other residual composites held in that external repository.

This process is like the way many distinct determinations from varied sources can be gathered into one, with their separate markings dissolved and then brought into a single coherent form; the multitude of prior determinations and shapes are brought to completion as one organized whole.

So it was also with this composite in the external repository: it too was shaped and fixed by the power of inward craving within it, gathered from many persuasive teachings and deliberations belonging to the residual elements of that ordered progression of cognitions.

The first design for producing this composite was threefold.

First, that the progression of cognitions might be lightened and purified of the burden within it. Just as the full outer arrangements had been relieved and purified of the burden from the mixed influences, so the progression itself was also relieved and purified of the burden and remainder held inside it.

Second, that there might be added a restraint and confinement upon the progression and its ordered varieties that are bound to it, so that when they press upward beyond their proper degree, the composite within external knowledges draws them back by a hard restraint, and they cannot rise. And when the powers governing that progression incline toward deceit and it enters their intention to flow down into the outermost degree, they cannot descend, because a fixed arrest is set upon the progression at the boundary of the outer arrangements. This is one restraint. Yet another restraint operates by constant supervision from vigilant guardings set over it, so that it is compelled into continual regulated motion.

Third, that all the general influxes of truth, and the diverse forms of understanding and love that surge from the circuit of external knowledges, together with the streams of thought that move through the outermost degree and return to what is general, and the descending influxes that terminate in ultimates, and the residues and renewals that come down with them—this general external repository might serve as a common reception and gathering place for all of these.

As for all the force and vitality that descends into this general repository, and for the inbreathing by which the composite draws that vitality into itself so as to agitate what is general: an interaction and fullness arises from its movement, tending toward purification; but the continuation of this sense is unclear, because the text breaks off.

fills.notes: The King of Glory “turned the three wheels” and thereby caused the wheels to be set and elevated. The correspondential sense requires establishment in a fixed ordered station (the higher arrangement “up above all the mountains”). The gap fits an adverbial phrase marking their being set in their proper position before the wind and washing act on them.

The waste from washing the star-wheel is cast into the inner sea “like … of the mountain.” The spiritual sense is a descent from an elevated state into an external one; the natural correspondence is a heavy piece falling from a height. “A stone of the mountain” is the tightest image for that downward casting and for the fixed, hardened remainder that will be formed.

After the repository’s ‘thought’ gathers the residue, it must be bound and stationed at the lowest, most external level (fixed in ultimates). “In the depths” matches the correspondential requirement: a fixing in the lowest general containant (the inner sea as external knowledges).

fills.fill: and the courses of the seven planets.
fills.notes: The seals named are measures of time and the ‘impression of the stars and the signs of the zodiac’; the oldest cosmological substrate regularly completes this set with the planetary courses as the immediate governors of sublunary changes. This also matches the spiritual translation’s ‘determinations of cognitions with their ordered varieties.’

The giant bears ‘doctrines and counsels of …’ and in ¶3 the residue explicitly comes from the washed-out star-wheel. The substrate logic is that the composite is the condensed remainder of that very wheel; thus the source must be named here as the wheel of the stars, not a later institutional or moral referent.

The sea ‘conceived him … for its part … it being his chief sculptor.’ The correspondential sense requires that the general repository not only receives but actively seizes and engages the residue to give it determinate form. “Conceived him and took hold of him” expresses reception plus formative appropriation in the oldest register.

fills.fill: in the work of his shaping;
fills.notes: The following clause explains why: ‘it being his chief sculptor and chief craftsman.’ The lacuna should specify the mode of participation—its share in the shaping process—before naming it as the primary artisan. This keeps the impersonal cosmological tone and matches the spiritual translation’s “took part in its formation.”

The example concludes the correspondential point: many stamped determinations dissolved and recast into one coherent organized whole. The oldest-layer wording should finish the analogy with unification of form rather than moralizing. This also matches the spiritual translation’s ‘brought into a single coherent form.’

The syntax “that he might disturb the sea [ ... a] fullness” demands a verbal bridge leading into “fullness.” The spiritual sense indicates ‘an interaction and fullness arises’; thus “there is … a fullness” is required. The surviving ‘a’ at the end aligns naturally with “a fullness.”

The spiritual translation preserves the required concept: an interaction arising from the composite’s movement and inbreathing. The natural-layer term that best fits the oldest substrate here is the straightforward “interaction,” naming the reciprocal agitation between sea and giant before mentioning “fullness.”

The clause “becomes between his movement [ ... ] purify” needs a connective introducing the telos of the arising interaction: it tends toward cleansing. “That will purify” matches both the natural sequence and the spiritual sense ‘tending toward purification.’

The final broken clause “but the sea …” in context contrasts the purifying tendency with the continued general agitation or ongoing receptivity of the repository. The oldest-layer closure most consistent with the preserved sense is that the sea’s motion or surging continues—hence “does not cease.” Exact object is lost, but the required opposition is persistence of the sea’s general state despite the purifying interaction.

assessment: Most gaps are constrained by the correspondential structure: residue from the star-wheel cast into the inner sea, gathered and fixed in the depths, then sealed with time-measures and astral determinations. The most uncertain restorations are ¶2 #1 (idiomatic placement of the wheels) and especially the final broken contrast in ¶12 #4, where only the general oppositional logic (purifying interaction versus continued sea-condition) can be recovered.
